text:
Aisha: CI red on PR #4128, intermittent failure in TestServeRetryPolicy on linux-amd64 CI job 8842. Fails ~1/8 runs. Can someone triage? :grimacing:
Jon: ack, can you paste the failure log & seed if any?
Aisha: here - failing assert in retry_backoff_test.go: line 142. Seed=0x7f2a9b, run args: `go test ./runtime -run TestServeRetryPolicy -v`
Aisha: ```
--- FAIL: TestServeRetryPolicy (0.05s)
    retry_backoff_test.go:142: expected 3 retries but got 1
    serve_test.go:73: last error: context deadline exceeded
FAIL
```
Diego: hmm sounds timing/nondeterminism. Does CI use the deterministic scheduler patch?
Aisha: no, this job uses standard runner image. Only noticed after the recent scheduler change in PR 4110.
Sam: I can try to repro locally. Quick question — can you rerun the job with `-count=100` or `GOMAXPROCS=2` to see frequency?
CI Bot: rerun triggered: https://ci.example.com/job/8842/rerun (initiated by Aisha) :repeat:
Jon: also try `-run TestServeRetryPolicy -count 500` locally, and `GODEBUG=schedtrace=100` to capture scheduling info.
Diego: if it's flaky because of real timeouts, we should mock the clock in that test or use a fake timer. Adding sleeps is brittle.
Aisha: I reproduced once with `go test -run TestServeRetryPolicy -count=50` — failed 2/50. Reproduced seed: 0x7f2a9b.
Sam: repro log shows the retry loop exited early due to a canceled context from an earlier goroutine. Might be a race where the timer fires and cancels whole request. Can you run `go test -race`?
Aisha: ran race with -count=10, no races reported, but still flaky.
Diego: next steps: 1) bisect to find the regressing commit, 2) add a deterministic timer to the test, 3) consider increasing internal backoff window or introducing jitter bounds.
Jon: for bisect, try `git bisect run ./scripts/ci-test.sh -- TestServeRetryPolicy` with the failing seed pinned. If it's nondet, narrow by disabling unrelated patches (e.g., scheduler change).
Sam: quick patch that helped me locally: replace `time.After` in test helper with `fakeClock.Advance(10*time.Millisecond)` and assert deterministic behavior. That made 200/200 passes locally. Not a final fix but good for test stability.
Aisha: thanks — I'll open a small PR with the fake-clock change and add an integration to run the stress `-count=200` in CI for this test. Trying to avoid masking a real bug though.
Diego: yes please include the bisect outcome in the PR description and tag @eng-runtime for review. Also add a TODO comment linking to a follow-up to inspect scheduler interaction.
Jon: :thumbsup: If anyone wants, I can babysit the bisect this afternoon.
Aisha: assigning to Diego for bisect, Sam for local repro notes. I'll upload the temp-fix PR and link back here. Thanks all :eyes:
CI Bot: job 8842 rerun completed: 3 failures out of 200 runs (log: https://ci.example.com/job/8842/log)
Aisha: copying logs into the PR and filing an issue: runtime#789 (will link).
